findings.title: Possible NPE when the 'Clients' resource-type resource cannot be resolved
findings.body: In hasPermission(ClientModel, String), when no resource exists for the client, the code falls back to AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceTypeResource(...). That method returns null when the realm's authorization schema is not supported/enabled or the resource was not found. The returned value is passed straight into policyStore.findByResource(server, resource) and then dereferenced via resource.getScopes(), so a null result causes a NullPointerException (HTTP 500) instead of simply denying access. Add a null check returning false.

findings.title: getClientsWithPermission includes the aggregate 'Clients' resource in the result set
findings.body: resourceStore.findByType(server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...) matches every resource whose type is "Clients", which includes the schema-created aggregate resource named "Clients" (created in AdminPermissionsSchema.init with name == type == "Clients"). If a permission is granted on the aggregate resource, the literal string "Clients" is added to the returned set of client ids. Callers interpret these entries as client identifiers, so this yields a bogus id (and, conversely, granting an all-clients permission does not expand into the actual client ids). Filter out the resource whose name equals the resource type and handle the all-clients case explicitly.

findings.title: getResourceName has no branch for the new Clients resource type
findings.body: getResourceName only resolves friendly names for the Users resource type. For permissions with resourceType "Clients" it falls through to resource.getDisplayName(), which is not set for resources created by getOrCreateResource (only name == client internal id is stored). As a result the admin API/UI will show null (or no name) for client-scoped permissions, instead of the clientId or "All clients". Add a Clients branch resolving the client by id, mirroring the Users handling.

findings.title: Removal cleanup listener now skipped when neither FGAP v1 nor v2 flag matches
findings.body: registerListener's body is now wrapped in `Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)`. Previously the role/client/group removal handlers always ran, cleaning up leftover authorization policies for deleted roles, clients and groups created while v1 was enabled. After this change, if an installation disables the v1 feature (e.g. switches to v2) any pre-existing v1 permission policies for removed roles/clients/groups are left orphaned in the database. If the gating is only meant to avoid the UnsupportedOperationException thrown by the new V2 classes, gate on "v2 not enabled" or make the V2 setPermissionsEnabled a no-op instead.

findings.title: Dead code and unused imports in new class
findings.body: getEvaluationContext(ClientModel, AccessToken) is private and never called, and the `logger` field, the static import of AdminPermissionManagement.TOKEN_EXCHANGE and the imports of Scope/ClientModelIdentity/DefaultEvaluationContext/EvaluationContext are unused. This dead code was presumably copied from ClientPermissions (token exchange) and should be removed to avoid suggesting token-exchange evaluation is supported here (canExchangeTo throws UnsupportedOperationException).
